What effect would Bernie Sanders tax plan increases have on the economy?

That depends on a lot of things, which were discussed in the article you took that image from. For the average person, those increases in taxes are offset (to a debatable degree) by the decrease in healthcare spending, childcare costs, college tuition, and other boons. If this results in more money in peoples' pockets, then that is good for the economy, as those people will likely spend it, stimulating the economy.

People who have large incomes don't generally spend what they get, they save it in various ways. There is contentious debate about how much their savings benefit the economy.

The most interesting part of the article you got this image from was about the capital gains tax. In my opinion, we should be discussing whether or not raising it would affect the economy, and how, and... whether maximizing government revenue, or maximizing stock market trade volume ought to really be the goal.

I read Vox's opinion...

The 10% tax increase on the lower\middle class is not going to put more money in peoples pockets. The only people that will benefit from this are the ones using 10k+ per year of healthcare, and those people are saving everything to pay for their illnesses.

Or paying out the nose for child care, or sending their children to college, or any combination of these and other things. But I didn't claim it would offset it completely, I merely said it would offset it to a debatable degree, and we should debate that.

Sockpuppets, or alts, have always plagued online communities, and they will continue to be used until there are reasonable measures taken against them. They are a critical problem on content aggregators because sockpuppet armies can easily be used to control the narrative of a subverse without blatantly deleting content or banning users. Dealing with the issue seems to be a necessary first step in creating a democratic online community, as democracy only works if each user only has one vote per submission/comment.

The problem is exaggerated by the fact that users have few ways of actually proving that it's happening, even when it most certainly does occur. And it's even harder to prevent than it is to retroactively punish, especially if you want to respect user privacy.

How do you think we ought to deal with the sockpuppet problem without violating user privacy or free expression?
